body.statement: For the exact late-ramp pair and every possibly randomized confidence set \(D_n\) measurable from \(O_n\), if \(\liminf_n\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}\Pr_{\sigma}(\tau_n^{\sigma}\in D_n)\ge0.95\), then for each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), \(\liminf_n\Pr_{\sigma}(\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge1/8)\ge\sqrt{1/2}-0.1=0.6071067811865475\ldots\).
body.justification: The theorem establishes an information bound for every honest confidence set from the complete logged experiment, not an estimator-specific implication of the HT limit.
body.gap: ShekharRamdas2023 treats i.i.d. bounded-mean width and HongLeungLi2020 treats diverging effective information; neither uses a shared adaptive void event with this exact finite-population constant.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a quantitative warning that nominally valid inference cannot be uniformly narrow when an arm receives only bounded cumulative allocation hazard.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(m_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), and define the common late-arm void event
\[
 V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\}.
\]
The predictable-randomization membership conclusion of Proposition \texttt{prop:late-ramp-membership}, together with \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair}, gives the deterministic conditional success probability \(c/t\).  Repeated use of the tower property, with each preceding product of assignment indicators measurable with respect to the preceding filtration, therefore yields under either sign
\[
 \eta_n:=\Pr_{\sigma}(V_n)
 =\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\left(1-\frac{c}{t}\right)
 =\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right).
\]
This calculation uses only the randomization law; the fixed-outcome conclusion of Proposition \texttt{prop:late-ramp-membership} ensures that the potential outcomes create no additional randomness.

We next evaluate the mass exactly enough for the asserted constant.  For \(0\le x<1\), elementary integration gives
\[
 0\le-\log(1-x)-x
 =\int_0^x\frac{s}{1-s}\,ds
 \le\frac{x^2}{2(1-x)}.
\]
Applying this with \(x=1/(2t)\), and using
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1{t^2}
 \le\frac{n-m_n}{(m_n+1)^2}=O(n^{-1}),
\]
gives
\[
 \log\eta_n
 =-\frac12\sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1t+o(1).
\]
For \(m_n\ge1\), monotonicity of \(x\mapsto1/x\) gives the elementary integral squeeze
\[
 \log\!\left(\frac{n+1}{m_n+1}\right)
 =\int_{m_n+1}^{n+1}\frac{dx}{x}
 \le\sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1t
 \le\int_{m_n}^{n}\frac{dx}{x}
 =\log\!\left(\frac{n}{m_n}\right).
\]
Both outer terms converge to \(\log2\), because \(m_n/n\to1/2\); hence the middle sum converges to \(\log2\).
Consequently,
\[
 \eta_n\longrightarrow \exp\{-\tfrac12\log2\}
 =2^{-1/2}=\sqrt{1/2}.
\]

The restrictions of the two complete-data laws to \(V_n\) are identical.  Indeed, deterministic conditional assignment probabilities imply, by the same tower-property induction, the same law for the entire assignment vector under both signs.  For \(t\le m_n\), \(t/n\le1/2=a_0\), so \(Y_{nt}^{+}(1)=Y_{nt}^{-}(1)=0\).  For \(t>m_n\), the event \(V_n\) forces the control outcome to be observed, and that outcome is zero under both signs.  Thus every observed outcome is zero on \(V_n\); the completed propensity log \((e_{nt})\) and regression log \((m_{nt})\) are also the same deterministic arrays under the two signs by \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair}.  Hence
\[
 \Pr_+\bigl((O_n,U)\in H,\,V_n\bigr)
 =\Pr_-\bigl((O_n,U)\in H,\,V_n\bigr)
 =:\nu_n(H)
\]
for every measurable \(H\), where equality continues to hold for the auxiliary randomization \(U\) because \(U\) is independent of the experiment and has the same law under both signs.  The common subprobability measure \(\nu_n\) has total mass \(\nu_n(\Omega)=\eta_n\).

For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), put
\[
 E_{\sigma,n}=\{\tau_n^{\sigma}\in D_n(O_n,U)\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}\Pr_{\sigma}(E_{\sigma,n}^{c}).
\]
The honesty premise is equivalent to
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le0.05.
\]
Since \(\nu_n\) is the restriction of the sign-
\(\sigma\) law to \(V_n\),
\[
 \nu_n(E_{\sigma,n}^{c})
 =\Pr_{\sigma}(V_n\cap E_{\sigma,n}^{c})
 \le\Pr_{\sigma}(E_{\sigma,n}^{c})
 \le\gamma_n.
\]
The union bound under the common subprobability measure now gives
\[
 \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})
 \ge \eta_n-2\gamma_n.
\]
On \(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n}\), the same reported set contains both deterministic causal targets.  Proposition \texttt{prop:late-ramp-membership} gives
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(D_n)
 \ge |\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-|\ge\frac18.
\]
Since \(\nu_n\) is dominated by either sign-specific probability measure, for each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 \Pr_{\sigma}\!\left(\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\frac18\right)
 \ge \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})
 \ge \eta_n-2\gamma_n.
\]
Taking lower limits and using the two limits already proved yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{\sigma}\!\left(\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\frac18\right)
 \ge \sqrt{1/2}-2(0.05)
 =\sqrt{1/2}-0.1
 =0.6071067811865475\ldots .
\]
This is an information bound for every measurable confidence set based on the complete log; no property of the Horvitz--Thompson estimator or of any distributional limit was used.

As a smallest-instance check, direct evaluation gives
\[
 (\Delta_1,\Delta_2,\Delta_3,\Delta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac29,\frac3{16}\right),
 \qquad
 (\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3,\eta_4)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac34,\frac58,\frac{35}{48}\right).
\]
Thus every one of the first four finite designs has the required target separation, while the exact void masses agree with the product formula whose limiting value supplies the theorem's constant.
